success_criteria: final pass count must NOT fall below 29/32
final pass count is expected to stay EQUAL; a rise needs separate proof, not silent acceptance
every run whose stall persisted across attempts must STILL fail
refutation_criteria: any persistent-stall run passes -> the retry converts real failures into passes and MUST be reverted
final pass count drops -> regression, MUST be reverted
false success becomes non-zero -> MUST be reverted
notes: Written before any source change. The existing plan-level retry already recovers 6 of 9 stall runs, so the honest increment of a skill-layer retry is latency and risk, not final pass rate. | 2026-11-11: factual basis corrected - a subset of release stalls are FALSE FAILURES (object released, confirmation lost) and the prediction must be re-derived before implementation.

superseded_basis.why: This pre-registration assumed every ACTUATOR_STALL_ON_RELEASE was a real release failure. Measurement on 32 validated runs showed at least 2 were the opposite: the object HAD been released and was inside the target zone, but the release confirmation failed, so place reported released=False err=25 while the world satisfied the goal.
superseded_basis.what_changes: For this sub-class, re-commanding the release cannot help - the gripper already opened. The defect is in the CONFIRMATION, not the actuation. The bounded_release_retry hypothesis therefore does not address the dominant observable failure mode.
superseded_basis.status_of_this_preregistration: NOT WITHDRAWN and NOT APPROVED. It stays requires_human_approval and must be re-derived from the corrected failure taxonomy before any code change is proposed.
superseded_basis.leakage: The prediction was fixed before any code change and was never used to manufacture a pass; no skill-layer file was modified.
